lesson_title: Two Dials, Five Graphs: Functions Exam Essentials
hook_text: Line, parabola, hyperbola, exponential, sine wave — ONE sentence controls them all.
clip_script: The letter q is the elevator. It lifts or lowers the entire graph without changing its shape. The parabola y equals x squared plus two is the basic bowl raised two units. On the trig graphs, q lifts the whole wave: the midline of y equals sine x plus one runs along y equals one instead of the x-axis. On the hyperbola and exponential, q moves the horizontal asymptote — the graph's forbidden height — from zero up to q. The letter a is the volume knob, with a twist: a negative a flips the graph upside down.
visual_style: Five graphs lined up in a gallery, a giant elevator dial lifting them all in sync, then a volume knob twisting and every shape flipping upside down at once.
pacing: Rhythmic dial turns hitting each family in sequence, building to the simultaneous flip.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and sketch any graph with one checklist.
